alignments.note: Cognate infinitive absolute expressing emphasis or continuation, with no distinct English rendering: 'forth' states outward motion, not the infinitive's force, so rule 56 does not assign it to this morpheme; the repeated occurrence is unrepresented under rule 22.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun 'He' (rule 17), discontinuous around the supplied relative.

The ASV subordinates a Hebrew main clause as a relative; no relative or article morpheme licenses 'that' (rule 55). Competing reading: 'He that' as a supplied headless-relative noun phrase joining s002 under rule 46.

'goeth' already renders הלך's going; 'forth' supplies an outward direction that no morpheme in this clause writes, so it is added under rule 44. Competing reading: keep 'goeth forth' as the finite verb's phrasal rendering; the separate particle is preferred because its outward direction is additional, not the infinitive absolute's emphasis or continuation.
Infinitive absolute rendered as a finite verb.

Construct מֶשֶׁךְ read by the ASV as 'sowing' (the margin's 'the measure of seed' read and set aside, rule 38); the chain is inverted in English, and the 'for' stands before the construct's own word, so it joins that unit. Competing reading: 'for' to the rectum s008 under rule 19.
Article on the rectum; ASV writes no 'the' (rule 29).
Finite verb with its auxiliary; 'again' is not the verb's (see added unit).
'come' already writes בּוֹא's lexeme and 'again' adds a return the Hebrew does not write (rule 44, as 'bring him back').
Supplied preposition and pronoun (ASV italic) with no morpheme for either; one added unit under rules 2 and 33.

review_notes: Margin 'bearing the measure of seed' read and set aside (rule 38).
